newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN THE FRENCH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN THE FRENCH LEAGUE.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the French first division (league position in parentheses, kickoff times GMT):

Monaco host lowly Lille with their minds on their UEFA semifinal clash with Internazionale next week. To keep their 10-point lead at the top over Paris St Germain, they should beware of Lille, who have replaced coach Jean-Michel Cavalli with Herve Gauthier.

Beaten in Auxerre last week, PSG probably surrendered any chance they had of lifting the title. The report that goalkeeper Bernard Lama failed a dope test for cannabis was another blow for the Parisians. Their task looks reasonably easy though against off-form Rennes, who have scored only two goals in their last six matches.

Cannes still need a couple of wins to leave the relegation zone behind but they fear neighbouring Nice, who have nothing to lose since they are already relegated. Nice, who have saved some of their season by making it to the Cup semifinals, will be without Liberian international James Debbah.

Lyon and Auxerre cannot afford to lose more points if they wish to stay in the race for UEFA Cup berths next season. Both have problems with their centre forwards. Lyon's Florian Maurice and Auxerre's Lilian Laslandes are recovering from injuries but should hold their places.

Metz hope to halt a recent bad run but the absence of international Robert Pires, Senegal's Amara Traore and Cameroon's Rigobert Song will not help them, especially as Le Havre can count on a full squad.

The clash between the two southern teams has become a classic of the season. They met in the Cup and in the League Cup and this will be their fourth tie this season. Bordeaux, who lead 2-1 so far, will be without striker Jean-Pierre Papin. Both teams are unbeaten in the league this year.

Unbeaten in their last 24 league matches, Nantes hope to come closer to their league record of 32 when they host Marseille. A win would probably save Marseille, who may be without Bulgaria's Iordan Letchkov, from relegation.
Without five first choice players, lowly Nancy look unlikely to disturb in-form Strasbourg, who shot to third on the table last week and have no players injured.
Guingamp, who qualified for the French Cup semifinals last week, are without injured striker Lionel Rouxel and goalkeeper Angelo Hugues for their home match against lowly Caen.

After a surprising start to the season, Bastia have slumped lately and have lost their last three away matches. But Lens, who are still not saved from relegation, will be without Titi Camara and Marc-Vivien Foe, both called in by their countries for World Cup qualifiers.
